Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and constraints from our side: 

Key constraints
- Data residency is non-negotiable: processing/storage must remain within the EU (we operate under strict GDPR and local regulator guidance).
- We cannot accept silent cross-region failover that moves persistent data or unencrypted payloads to the US. Short-lived compute in other regions may be acceptable only for non-PII and with explicit agreement.
- Procurement will evaluate Dedicated (preferred) and Private VPC. Hosted API could be considered if we get a written guarantee about EU-only routing and a clear escalation/fallback plan.

Questions
1) For Hosted API: can you confirm whether regional endpoints guarantee data-at-rest and network egress remain in region? Are there options to disable cross-region fallback?
2) For Dedicated: what level of logical separation do we get (single-tenant GPU pool vs tenant-aware scheduling)?
3) For Private VPC: do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key custody?

I've cc'd procurement. They'll expect SOC2 and a short list of required network/IP ranges. I'll share our internal security contact after procurement confirms.

Best,

Hi Sofie — quick technical answers to your questions below; happy to do a live run-through on a call.

1) Hosted API regional guarantees
- We operate an EU-hosted API in eu-west (Frankfurt/Amsterdam pools). For Hosted customers we persist data in-region by default; backups and snapshots are configured to remain in-region for accounts with residency requirements.
- Cross-region fallback (automatic routing to a different region) is an opt-in feature for resilience; for accounts with residency requirements we can set policy to disable cross-region fallback entirely. That said, some managed services (third-party backups, global logs) require explicit contract language to fully avoid any cross-border telemetry — we can provide that language.

2) Dedicated
- Dedicated gives you a dedicated GPU pool logically isolated to Nordbank. Workloads are scheduled only on the dedicated pool; we do not co-locate other tenants' models on your cluster. It's still managed by Redwood but with tenant isolation and EU-only networking.

3) Private VPC / on-prem
- We support Private VPC deployment with customer-managed network peering and optional customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key via supported KMS integrations). On-prem installations are also supported for fully air-gapped needs, though they increase onboarding time and ops responsibilities.

Security artifacts and network requirements
- SOC2_summary.pdf (attached in Marissa's email) covers relevant controls. I can also provide a short network_req.txt that lists required IP ranges/ports for outbound/inbound.

Proposed technical call
- I'll run through the EU-only config, demonstrate a non-fallback policy, and walk through the Dedicated vs Private network diagrams. Available windows: 2026-09-22 09:00-11:00 CEST or 2026-09-23 10:00-12:00 CEST.

I'll attach a network_requirements_diagram.png to illustrate VPC peering and firewall rules.
